sources.entry: Signal Desktop - Electron app that links with your Signal Android or Signal iOS app.

summary.one_liner: Signal Desktop is an Electron-based desktop messaging app that links to the Signal app on Android or iOS so you can message from Windows, macOS, or Linux.
summary.what_it_does: The README describes Signal Desktop as a companion to Signal on Android or iOS, letting users send and receive messages from Windows, macOS, and Linux computers. It points to a production release and a beta release that users can install. Support is handled through a support site and a community forum, and bug reports go through the issue tracker after searching for duplicates. The README also covers contributing (see CONTRIBUTING.md), in-app donations, and a cryptography export notice. It does not include build or run instructions in the text provided.
use_cases: secure messaging on a desktop computer
chat from Windows, macOS, or Linux while using a phone
testing the beta version of Signal
contributing to an open-source encrypted chat client
how_to_run: Install the production version from the Signal website or use the beta version (download details are not in the README text provided).
notable: Pairs with the Signal mobile app on Android or iOS rather than running as a standalone account
Runs on Windows, macOS, and Linux
Offers both production and beta release channels
Operated by Signal Technology Foundation, a 501(c)(3) nonprofit
caveats: Requires an existing Signal account on Android or iOS to link with
The README provided gives no build or setup steps for developers
